cohort: The study included 499 mother-neonate pairs from Madagascar and Cambodia, with stool samples collected at delivery from mothers and during the first three days of life from neonates.
finding: Maternal gut carriage accounts for only 16.5% of neonatal ESBL-PE acquisition, challenging the paradigm that it is the primary source of early neonatal ESBL-PE colonization.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery is associated with an increased risk of neonatal ESBL-PE acquisition from sources other than the mother.
